working_on.feature: AI Text & Summarize Best Practices Fix
working_on.task: Completed Phases 01-03: Immediate TTS Stop & Progress Reset, Scroll Auto-Reset, Coroutine Cancellation Handling & Unit Tests
working_on.notes: Full best practices alignment complete. Implemented immediate TTS service stop (ACTION_STOP), highlight clearing, and progress reset to 0% upon clicking AI actions. Added 3 comprehensive unit tests in AiTextButtonTest.kt with 100% tests passing.

recent_changes.description: Phase 03: Added unit tests for TTS stop, scroll reset, and coroutine cancellation in AiTextButtonTest.kt.
Phase 02: Coroutine cancellation safety: rethrow CancellationException and guard against null _binding.
Phase 01: Stop TTS immediately and reset scroll to (0, 0) upon clicking AI Text / Summarize.
Phase 04: Added integration verification and finalized full test suite build passing.

errors_encountered.error: Fragile _binding access in coroutine catch/main blocks could throw NPE if view destroyed during API calls
errors_encountered.solution: Check if (_binding == null) before UI touches and rethrow CancellationException

errors_encountered.error: Asynchronous SharedPreferences apply() calls caused flaky race conditions in integration tests
errors_encountered.solution: Switched all writes in ModelQuotaManager from apply() to synchronous commit()

errors_encountered.error: Robolectric mock leakages in static classes caused downstream test suite failures
errors_encountered.solution: Added global unmockkAll() in @After blocks in verification tests

decisions_made.reason: Prevents out-of-sync audio reading old text while new text is being generated/replaced.

decisions_made.decision: Reset scroll position to (0, 0) on new content
decisions_made.reason: Ensures user starts reading from top of text instead of an arbitrary scroll offset.
Swallowing CancellationException breaks Kotlin structured concurrency and lifecycle cancellation.
MD5(ModelName_ApiKey) separates quota statuses across keys cleanly and avoids cross-key cache collision.
Using commit() over apply() ensures immediate I/O persistence, avoiding asynchronous state race conditions during heavy JUnit tests.
